title: 5 Week Course: The Work on Inadequacy (Timing Option A) Price - Sliding Scale
description:
The Mindful Stream
To celebrate 5 years of The Work Runs Free, Emrys has created The Work on Inadequacy. Over 5 weeks, we explore different ways the experience of inadequacy shows up in our lives, using The Work to investigate our experience.

Sign up form: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeQVso7QaCu9ubv5E_74f50c6vvp2nt7zx8zMWnlGkwaNIYMw/viewform?usp=preview)
Detailed Course Outline: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eQYHU2jgRlNoO_XZDEjj08EhT8jeHk0h2zAOnEoglgM/edit?usp=sharing)

**Sliding Scale Price:** $120 — Accessible rate / $150 — Standard rate / $180 — Pay it forward

**Week 1 — I'm Not Good Enough:** The fundamental inadequacy story.
**Week 2 — Comparison:** Measuring ourselves against other people.
**Week 3 — I'm a Fraud / They'll Find Me Out:** Imposter feelings, competence and exposure.
**Week 4 — Being Loved, Accepted & Enough:** Inadequacy in relationships, belonging and being seen by others.
**Week 5 — Achievement & Where I Should Be:** Success, progress, potential and the feeling that we should be further along.

The course gently moves from the broader experience of inadequacy into increasingly specific areas where it can show up in our lives.

As we gently move into each topic, you are invited to become still and notice any stressful thought, belief or experience that arises through the inquiry, and to write it down — either on a notepad or in an electronic document.

Each session explores one stressful thought, or “one-liner,” using a format known as Popcorn Work. This is the same approach Emrys uses in his weekly *[The Work Runs Free](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/)* group. Everyone participates in their own inquiry, but there is no expectation to share. You are equally welcome to keep your inquiry entirely private, if that feels right for you.

The group is deliberately small, with a maximum of 10 participants, allowing us to explore together while each person remains connected to their own experience.

Please note that this is a paid course. In order to join you must register for the event (sign up form above). The Zoom link for this event will be sent around 24 hours after registration and payment has been made.

**To book a free introductory private session of The Work with Emrys, [click here](https://calendly.com/mindfulnesswithemrys/onehoursession)[.](https://mindfulnesswithemrys.business.site/)**

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

👟 **Court Priority:** Those who are signed up and show up by 9 AM will have top priority for court space. Those who show up later have second priority while those who are wait-listed will have third priority. This is only in the event that we have to rotate people in.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: Let's Walk!! Brookdale Park
description:
Let's Walk!!
If entering from Bellevue Avenue and park in the first parking lot on the left. We will be gathering near the playground area.

if entering from Watchung Ave, park and walk up to the upper parking lot near the playground area.

We will be walking the outer path. There are several break-off points if you do not want to walk the entire path.

The walk will be about an hour or at least 3-4 miles.

Wear comfortable shoes!

Please plan to arrive 5 minutes early. The walk will start promptly.

Brookdale Park offers the public access to both passive and active recreational activities as well as picturesque vistas. Trails for walking and running, lush groves and extensive lawns, playgrounds, sports fields, track facilities, tennis courts, an archery range and stadium grandstand are just some of the numerous attractions that make Brookdale Park a magnet for nature lovers, families, and physical fitness enthusiasts for miles around.

title: DJ Rafe Gomez presents Danceteria REWIND at Porta
location: Porta Montclair, 499 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
DJ Rafe Gomez, host of the popular Twitch channel Danceteria REWIND, will present an immersive sonic and visual re-creation of the famed NYC nightclub Danceteria at Porta in Montclair.  The free event, which will be the tri-state area’s official debut of Rafe’s multimedia performance, will take place on Saturday, 11/28, 499 Bloomfield Avenue, from 9pm to 1am. 
Danceteria was a New York hotspot from 1979 to 1986.  It was famous for embracing iconic art (Keith Haring worked at the club as a waiter, Kenny Scharf was a member of the performance troupe, and Jean-Michel Basquiat painted murals), video, fashion, and music.  It’s also where LL Cool J, the Beastie Boys, RuPaul, Debi Mazar, and Madonna got their starts. 
This year, Danceteria has been trending:  Madonna released a #1 hit single titled “Danceteria” that chronicled her adventures there, and the UK synth duo Soft Cell’s new album “Danceteria” explores the early 80s downtown NYC scene that inspired their musical journey. 
Gomez’s Twitch show, which launched in 2023 and streams weekly on Thursday nights, has over 60,000 global followers.  Using playlists of Danceteria’s original DJs, he serves up a beat-matched flow that replicates the club’s distinctive multi-genre mix of rap, electro, EDM, 70s funk, Afrobeat, Latin boogaloo, 60s garage rock and bubblegum, punk, reggae, new wave, disco, and more. 
Along with attracting international followers to his Twitch mix, Gomez has also garnered attention from the overseas art world.  He’s currently curating soundtracks for exhibitions in Italy and Japan that will showcase works by the superstar artists who were part of the Danceteria community. 
“Danceteria was a five-floor supermarket of style where gays, straights, artists, goths, skinheads, lost uptowners, curious bridge and tunnel kids, weirdos from outer space, drag queens, and world-changing creatives of all kinds got together,” says Gomez.  ”For everyone who was lucky enough to visit the club, my Porta gig will bring back great memories.  And for those who never had the chance to check it out, prepare for a fantastic trip.”

title: Chester County Horse-Shoe and More Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this point to point hike in rural Chester County Pennsylvania, featuring some prominent trails including the Horse-Shoe Trail, as well as other connections!
I have planned this one specifically because it is a Sunday that hunting isn't permitted in some of the preserves along the way, and because most of the route is pleasant but within safety zones.
After meeting at Bryn Coed, we will shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to our start point, at Highland Farm Park.
We'll start by walking some of the trails to the north, through fields and a wood line, out into a development.
We'll cut through the development and then out to the Pickering Creek Trail.
We'll take the Station Blvd Trail north to the Eagle Farms Trail east, then turn onto the pleasant Chester Springs Road.
The lightly trafficked road will lead us to the Horse-Shoe Trail where we last left off on it.
We'll follow Horse-Shoe Trail east for a bit, and then turn off at Bodine Road.
We'll follow a short road bit to the Hickory Trail which takes us north more.
From the Elbow Road, we'll reach the Binky Lee Preserve and pass through fields and woods. We'll exit the north side from that, and then follow some more back roads for a bit.
Lightly used Kimberton Road and Flint Road will take us to Bryn Coed Preserve for the last leg of the hike.
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374
Distance will be about 15 miles.

Sunday, November 29, 10:00 – 12:00: Oakdale Loop.

A post-Thanksgiving tradition, this 2-3 mile hike **MAY** help get rid of some of that extra pie.

Meet at: Oakdale parking area on Cherry Lane right across the road from the reservoir.

Leader: Lou Nocito, 973-953-7099

\*\*\* In registering for this or any other South Mountain Conservancy (SMC) programs in 2026 online, I hereby release and agree to hold the SMC, its volunteers, staff and Board of Trustees, harmless from and waive on behalf of myself, my heirs, and any personal representatives any and all causes of action, claims, demands, damages, costs, expenses and compensation for damage or loss to myself and/or property that may be caused by any act, or failure to act, in this SMC activity, or that may otherwise arise in any way in connection with any other SMC activity. I understand that this release discharges the SMC from any liability or claim that I, my heirs, or any personal representatives, may have against the SMC with respect to any bodily injury, illness, death, medical treatment, or property damage that may arise from, or in connection to, any SMC program. This liability waiver and release extends to the SMC along with Essex County and its staff and any other affiliated organization or SMC partner. I also understand that by signing below I approve the possible use of photos of me at this SMC event on social media or in promotional materials.
**BY REGISTERING FOR THIS HIKE I attest I am in good health and attest that I: Am not experiencing any symptoms of illness such as cough, shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, fever, chills, repeated shaking with chills, muscle pain, headache, sore throat, or new loss of taste or smell.**
**Am following all CDC recommended guidelines, above, and limiting my exposure to the novel coronavirus/COVID-19.**
\# Arrival\, Weather\, & Cancellations
Please come to the starting point 10 minutes ahead of time so the hike can start promptly. Times are our best estimates; they can vary depending on conditions, and the size and pace of a group. If you have any questions, call the leader. **Temperatures above 90 degrees and steady rain cancels, but intermittent drizzle does not. You will *not* be notified.** **Bring water. Wear hiking boots, preferably waterproof with good soles and traction devices and bring poles (optional).** Dogs are not allowed on hikes unless specified.
These hikes are publicized first to SMC members and then advertised to the public one week before a hike. There is a limit of 25 participants, so pre-registration is required at least two days before a hike to sign the liability waiver online and allow lists to be sent to hike leaders. If you have registered and then find you cannot attend, please cancel your order online. **Repeated no shows without prior cancellation will result in removal from list.**
**To become a current member visit [[https://www.somocon.org/membership/](https://www.somocon.org/membership/)]([https://www.somocon.org/membership/](https://www.somocon.org/membership/)).**

title: Perspectives on Human Trafficking Series: Office of the Attorney General
description:
Perspectives on Human Trafficking: Office of the New Jersey Attorney General
Join the Global Center on Human Trafficking (GCHT) at Montclair State University for two upcoming presentations featuring representatives from the New Jersey Office of the Attorney General. These sessions will explore human trafficking in New Jersey, including victim-centered responses, online exploitation, and emerging challenges for law enforcement.
Both events are free and open to all, with options to attend in person or virtually.
November 18, 2026 | Sexual Violence Unit
Time: 3:45 PM – 5:00 PMLocation: Calcia Hall, Room 140Presenter: Kathleen Friess, Program & Training Coordinator, Office of the New Jersey Attorney General
Drawing on more than 20 years of experience in the field, Kathleen Friess will provide an overview of human trafficking in New Jersey, including how to recognize potential indicators, understand vulnerabilities, and respond appropriately.
The presentation will also highlight New Jersey's efforts to address human trafficking through a victim-centered, trauma-informed approach.
November 30, 2026 | Cyber Bureaus
Time: 12:00 PM – 1:20 PMLocation: Calcia Hall, Room 140Presenter: Laura Magnone, Bureau Chief of the Human Trafficking and Cyber Bureaus, Office of the New Jersey Attorney General
Join Laura Magnone for a presentation exploring online exploitation from a legal and law enforcement perspective, including approaches to investigation and prosecution, and emerging challenges facing the field.

Hosted by: College of Humanities and Social Sciences (CHSS), Global Center on Human Trafficking

Additional Information can be found at: https://montclair.campuslabs.com/engage/event/12986028

title: DETROIT JAZZ Documentary Screening at Montclair State University FREE 6PM W/FILMMAKERS
location: Montclair State University Presentation Hall College of Communications and Media, 1 Normal Ave, Montclair, 07043, United States
description:
Montclair State University’s College of Communications Film Forum and the Music Department present: 
A Film Screening of Emerita Professor Roberta Friedman’s the new feature documentary: 
The Best of the Best: Jazz from Detroit
with Q&A w/Filmmakers Dan Loewenthal, Roberta Friedman, and writer Stryker 
Monday Night November 30th, 6PM-8:45PM. at College of Communication Building’s Presentation Hall. 
Synopsis: 
The Best of the Best: Jazz from Detroit chronicles the defining impact of Detroit’s innovative and influential jazz legacy and the iconic city that produced it. Inspired by Mark Stryker’s 2019 book, Jazz from Detroit, the 90-minute documentary weaves a compelling historical and cultural tapestry through the 20th and 21st centuries. Set within Detroit’s dramatic rise and fall as an industrial power and the struggles and triumphs of its creative and resilient African American community, the film connects the dots between the city’s history and Black musical excellence. 
Website: https://www.jazzfromdetroitfilm.com/ (See Trailer here. ) 
Directions:
Park in the Red Hawk deck, and walk to the center of campus – located directly across from the library is the CCOM building and inside the door on the left is the Presentation Hall.

Each year, our graduating class participates in a proud Class Gift tradition where members of the class invest in the University by supporting areas of Montclair State University that are most important to them. We invite the Class of 2026 to come together to show your support!
All gifts to Montclair count! Make your gift to any area of campus you feel most passionate about – such as the Emergency Book Fund, The Red Hawk Pantry, your school or college, The Fund for Montclair State or athletic program.

For a gift of $40, celebrate this milestone with your family, friends and colleagues by having your message displayed on the screen at the Commencement you will be participating in, and receive a customized philanthropy cords.

Graduates can also arrange to pick up their philanthropy cords in the Overlook Corporate Center, 150 Clove Road, Little Falls, NJ during business hours, Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. Philanthropy cords can also be mailed to those who cannot pick it up. description:

Requirements:

Volunteers must be Food Safe Certified to participate.
Complete the certification by following the step-by-step instructions provided in this link.

title: Spend the Holidays in The Twilight Zone
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a free Adult School class. 

Rod Serling wrote a few stories for The Twilight Zone about the holiday spirit and
specifically, about Christmas. Born on December 25th in 1924, Rod was known to often
say, ”I came as a present unwrapped.” Though Rod was Jewish, he and his family
enjoyed celebrating Christmas among friends and neighbors in his hometown of
Binghamton, NY.


Two of his wonderfully creative holiday episodes will be presented and discussed in the
upcoming micro-marathon.


The first is entitled, “The Night of the Meek”: S2:E11
A downtrodden, drunken department store Santa angers his employers and is fired from
his job. He wanders aimlessly in the streets of the city until he finds a magic sack that is
filled with gifts that can fulfill everyone’s wish, including his. Art Carney is stellar as the
Santa Claus that finds his “True North”.

The second is entitled, “Five Characters in Search of an Exit”: S3:E14
The title tells the story. An ensemble cast of characters in a very strange, nondescript
place don’t who they are, where they are and why they are there. What they need is to
determine how they can escape their surroundings. When they reach the exit, all
questions are answered.

title: 5 Week Course: The Work on Inadequacy (Timing Option A) Price - Sliding Scale
description:
The Mindful Stream
To celebrate 5 years of The Work Runs Free, Emrys has created The Work on Inadequacy. Over 5 weeks, we explore different ways the experience of inadequacy shows up in our lives, using The Work to investigate our experience.

Sign up form: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeQVso7QaCu9ubv5E_74f50c6vvp2nt7zx8zMWnlGkwaNIYMw/viewform?usp=preview)
Detailed Course Outline: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eQYHU2jgRlNoO_XZDEjj08EhT8jeHk0h2zAOnEoglgM/edit?usp=sharing)

**Sliding Scale Price:** $120 — Accessible rate / $150 — Standard rate / $180 — Pay it forward

**Please note: the timing of Timing Option A will go back one hour from Sat Nov 7th onwards to 6AM PDT / 9AM EDT**

**Week 1 — I'm Not Good Enough:** The fundamental inadequacy story.
**Week 2 — Comparison:** Measuring ourselves against other people.
**Week 3 — I'm a Fraud / They'll Find Me Out:** Imposter feelings, competence and exposure.
**Week 4 — Being Loved, Accepted & Enough:** Inadequacy in relationships, belonging and being seen by others.
**Week 5 — Achievement & Where I Should Be:** Success, progress, potential and the feeling that we should be further along.

The course gently moves from the broader experience of inadequacy into increasingly specific areas where it can show up in our lives.

As we gently move into each topic, you are invited to become still and notice any stressful thought, belief or experience that arises through the inquiry, and to write it down — either on a notepad or in an electronic document.

Each session explores one stressful thought, or “one-liner,” using a format known as Popcorn Work. This is the same approach Emrys uses in his weekly *[The Work Runs Free](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/)* group. Everyone participates in their own inquiry, but there is no expectation to share. You are equally welcome to keep your inquiry entirely private, if that feels right for you.

The group is deliberately small, with a maximum of 10 participants, allowing us to explore together while each person remains connected to their own experience.

Please note that this is a paid course. In order to join you must register for the event (sign up form above). The Zoom link for this event will be sent around 24 hours after registration and payment has been made.

**To book a free introductory private session of The Work with Emrys, [click here](https://calendly.com/mindfulnesswithemrys/onehoursession)[.](https://mindfulnesswithemrys.business.site/)**

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Amedeo Modigliani: Bohemian of Montmartre and Montparnasse
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. You can register here. 

Amedeo Modigliani, painter and sculptor, was born in Italy to a middle class, cultured Jewish family. He spent most of his tragically short life in France among the avant-garde artists of bohemian Paris. He is known for portraits and nudes in a contemporary style characterized by the elongation of faces and figures. Come and hear about this quintessentially unconventional artist and see many of his ravishing paintings and expressive sculptures. Some of his works are featured in the outstanding upcoming exhibition at the Brooklyn Museum, From Cezanne to Modigliani.

title: Accounting Society - KPMG
description:
KPMG is a prominent global network of independent firms delivering professional audit, tax, and advisory services. As one of the prestigious "Big Four" accounting firms, it operates across roughly 140 countries and employs over 270,000 professionals worldwide. The organization was officially formed in 1987 through the merger of Peat Marwick International and Klynveld Main Goerdeler, with its name representing the initials of its foundational partners. Instead of functioning as a single multinational corporation, KPMG is structured as a network of distinct, locally managed member firms. Its primary client base includes major corporations, government agencies, and non-profit institutions seeking regulatory compliance and strategic business consulting. Through this decentralized model, the firm maintains a massive footprint in global financial compliance and corporate restructuring.

title: Montclair Story Salon: Tradition! for Family Promise
location: First Congregational Church, 40 South Fullerton Ave., Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
Montclair Story Salon proudly presents Tradition!, an evening of storytelling, music, and live art on Wednesday, December 2, 2026, at 7:00 PM in the sanctuary at First Congregational Church in Montclair. This special fundraising event will benefit Family Promise of Essex County, an organization dedicated to helping families experiencing homelessness and housing insecurity find stability, secure safe housing, and build brighter futures. The evening will feature stories from:
• Farnoosh Torabi – Financial journalist, bestselling author, and host of the So Money podcast and the beloved Montclair Pod.
• George Oliphant – Emmy Nominated Host of NBC’s George to the Rescue.
• Henry H. Neff – bestselling author of the bestselling Tapestry series.
• Kim Coleman Foote – award-winning author of Coleman Hill.
• Live music: Ryan Hobler.
• Live art: Ling Chen, creating original artwork during the event.
• Host and MC: Liz Samuel, founder and producer of Montclair Story Salon.
Montclair Story Salon is grateful for the generous support of its community sponsors, including Elaine Pardalos of Brown Harris Stevens NJ Real Estate, Ironbound Farm Market and Watchung Booksellers, whose commitment helps make these community-centered events possible.
Join us for an unforgettable evening of stories, music, art, and community in support of families in need.

title: Poland Trip Information Meeting
description:
**Shomrei is Planning a Trip to Poland - Join us for a meeting where you will have a chance to learn more.**   
  
  
**The Trip**  
A Journey Honoring Jewish Life in Poland, Past and Present  
October 25 - November 2, 2027  
Join Rabbi Julie and fellow congregants for the trip of a lifetime as we explore 1,000 years of Jewish life in Poland, together as a community.  
  
**Purpose of this Meeting**  
This meeting will help everyone better understand the trip, learn more and ask questions. This meeting will be the ONLY in person chance to do so BEFORE registration opens in January.   
  
**Who should attend**  
The meeting is open to everyone who is considering the trip, even those who did not submit the interest form.   
  
**RSVP required** (Contact the Shomrei Office for the organizer's email.)  
You will be emailed the itinerary and other trip information after you register. Please review the these materials before the meeting.

title: Ink and Insight: Writing for Mental Health and Happiness
location: Montclair Main - Tower Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult school class. Please register here.

Journaling is an incredible tool for nurturing mental health and finding happiness. It allows us to reduce stress, release emotions, build mindfulness, and gain self-awareness—especially when it comes to identifying unhealthy patterns or habits. There are countless ways to approach journaling, each offering its own unique benefits to support better mental well-being.

In this two-session workshop, we’ll explore various journaling methods and delve into the specific advantages of each. Together, we’ll even dedicate time to put pen to paper and experience the therapeutic power of journaling firsthand.

title: Weekly Food Recovery Initiative
description:
Join our weekly Food Recovery events, where dedicated volunteers and members gather to make a difference in our community. Each week, participants help collect perfectly good leftover food from Gourmet Dining and transport it to Blanton. There, the food is repackaged into individual microwavable containers and stocked in the food pantry, providing meals for those in need throughout the week. 
To Participate: RSVP to attend the event each week. Meet in Blanton Hall Residence Hall Kitchenette in the Communal Area (Tell them you are working with Food Recovery), Sign in via Event Pass and your set!
Requirements:

Volunteers must be Food Safe Certified to participate.
Complete the certification by following the step-by-step instructions provided in this link.
Once certified, email your certification to foodrecoverynetwork@sgamsu.org to confirm your eligibility to participate.

Your involvement helps reduce food waste and insecurity while supporting individuals in our community who are in need. We look forward to your participation!*Please Note: This event end time is dependent on the amount of food given. You can estimate for max of hour and a half for recoveries.

Hosted by: EATS by Gourmet Dining, Food Recovery Network, Red Hawk Pantry

title: Book Talk: 20 Over 60 by Beth Weinhouse and David Galef
description:
In their new anthology 20 OVER 60 (Regal House; October 6, 2026), editors Beth Weinhouse and David Galef—also co-editors of the
anthology 20 OVER 40—present a portrait of later life that is consistently overlooked, in a culture obsessed with youth. The twenty short stories—including ones by Joyce Carol Oates, Paul Theroux, and Jane Gardam—are vibrant, moving, and often hilarious, capturing the texture of life after sixty in all its complexity.

Among the characters readers will meet: a retired couple whose hobby is stealing pepper mills from high-end restaurants, a woman juggling her husband and ex-husband staying in the same hospital, a futuristic nursing home whose designers become its unhappy residents, an older woman trying her hand at online dating, and a grandfather helping his granddaughter scatter her mother's ashes. These smart and poignant stories make the case that the years after sixty are as strange, surprising, and vivid as the decades that came before—and that readers living it deserve to see themselves on the page.

In an early review, Library Journal called 20 OVER 60 "remarkable," adding, "The editors succeed in creating an outstanding anthology that emphasizes that life continues to have vibrancy and significance after 60."

About the Co-Editors
Beth Weinhouse has been an editor at many mainstream magazines, including Self, Parenting, Prevention, Redbook, and Reader's Digest. She' s written feature articles and book reviews for New York Newsday, the Los Angeles Times Magazine, Travel & Leisure, Town & Country, Columbia Magazine, and more. Her first book was The Healthy Traveler, about maintaining health away from home. Her second book, co-written with Leslie Laurence, was Outrageous Practices, about how gender bias can threaten women's health. More at bethweinhouse.com.

David Galef has published over a dozen books, including the novel Flesh, the short story collection My Date with Neanderthal Woman, the children' s book Tracks, Japanese Proverbs: Wit and Wisdom, and Brevity: A Flash Fiction Handbook. Day job: English professor and creative writing program director at Montclair State University. He's also the editor of Vestal Review, the longest-running flash fiction magazine on the planet. Find him at davidgalef.com.

title: Library Speakers Consortium - Sparks, Shadows, and Epic Romantasy with Helen Scheuerer
description:
You must register here to attend:  https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/224402



Join us virtually for a downright intoxicating conversation with bestselling fantasy author Helen Scheuerer as we delve into her thrilling new novel, Kiss of the Black Flame.

Some bargains are sealed with blood. Others with fire. The deadliest are sealed with a kiss...

Saige Grayson has always believed stories could heal—even when her own body refuses to. As the most promising bookbinder in the capital, she’s learned to work through chronic pain and crushing debt, restoring other people’s treasures while trying not to fall apart herself. But when the man she owes decides her rare talent is worth more than her payments, Saige is traded to the Azkari—an immortal race forged by the gods for war—and imprisoned in their ancient stronghold.

Her only chance of survival lies with Archer, a fallen Azkari general imprisoned beside her—cursed, dangerous, and impossible to ignore. He offers her a way out, and in return, Saige must help him retrieve and restore an ancient book. But the book is made of living magic, powerful enough to stop a great evil—or unleash it. And as Saige works with Archer, the tome begins to awaken something dark and dangerous—both in the realm and within her.

As their enemies close in and buried memories resurface, Saige and Archer must decide what they’re willing to sacrifice: their freedom, their fragile trust…or the spark that could ignite the world.

Register now to take part in the magic–and the spice–of Helen’s newest book!

About the Author: 

Helen Scheuerer is a Sunday Times (London) bestselling author best known for her romantasy series, The Legends of Thezmarr and The Ashes of Thezmarr. Her work has been highly praised for its strong, flawed female characters and its action-packed plots. Helen’s love of writing and books led her to pursue a creative writing degree and a Master's of Publishing. She has been a full-time author since 2018 and is constantly dreaming up new stories.

title: 🥾 Let's Hike!! at Garret Mountain
description:
Let's Walk!!
Garret Mountain Yellow and White Loop Trail is a heavily trafficked loop trail located near Woodland Park, New Jersey that features a lake and is good for all skill levels. The trail offers a number of activity options and is best used from March until October.

**PLEASE ARRIVE 5 MINUTES EARLY SO WE CAN START ON TIME!**

We will hike a moderate 3 miles. This is **not** a paved trail, please do **not** wear sneakers.

We will meet in the **Auto Overlook** parking lot. It’s a one way, you will pass the equestrian, Lambert Tower before reaching the sign for AUTO OVERLOOK.

As always, we will go at a moderate pace and won’t leave anyone behind. But **please be considerate** of others if you don't think you will be able to hike at a moderate pace for the duration.

[https://www.google.com/maps/place/Parking+lot,+Paterson,+NJ+07503/@40.9057189,-74.1750062,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x89c2fdd38a2aa1a1:0x526711cb124756e2!8m2!3d40.905813!4d-74.1750982!16s%2Fg%2F11fx7w406f?hl=en-US&entry=ttu](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Parking+lot,+Paterson,+NJ+07503/@40.9057189,-74.1750062,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x89c2fdd38a2aa1a1:0x526711cb124756e2!8m2!3d40.905813!4d-74.1750982!16s%2Fg%2F11fx7w406f?hl=en-US&entry=ttu)

Rain or extreme weather will cancel the event.

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap.

title: The Space for Words - Literary Open mic with NJ Poetry Circle
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
The Space for Words – Literary Open mic hosted with the NJ Poetry Circle
Saturday December 5  |  Doors open at 7:30, start time 8 pm  |  $10 for everyone 
This event is usually held on the last Friday of every month.  The Space is transitioning to a new location, so this schedule is different through the end of the year.  We will resume the last Friday schedule at the new location in Wellmont Plaza in January. 
Hey writers, poets, and storytellers!  Come share your art with us at The Space for Words Open Mic Night. Whether you’re a seasoned author or just getting started, this is your chance to share your work in front of a supportive and inspiring audience. 
Bring your poetry, short stories, or excerpts from your latest work — the stage is yours! The Space is a safe place to try out new material, read old favorites, experiment with a different genre, and even to sing a song if inspiration strikes you. Each performer gets a maximum of 5 minutes to read, and at the end we take time to socialize and vibe with one another. 
Come for the words, stay for the community. The Space for Words has grown into an amazing community of writers supporting one another. This event is open to all levels and all genres, so whether you write fiction, non-fiction, memoir, or poetry, we want to hear from you. It’s all about celebrating the power of storytelling in a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere. All of our open mic nights are always inclusive. 
Anyone who puts their name in the bucket upon entry gets a shot at the mic, and has a maximum of 5 minutes. Depending on how many people sign up and if time allows, we can have people come up a second time. 
Audience members are, as always, a welcome and vital part of these performances. 
If you have published books that you would like to sell, bring some copies and be prepared to accept payment. 
General guidelines: 

Hate speech of any kind is never allowed and will be shut down.
Violence or references to physical harm to others will be shut down.

BYOB is welcome, and some light snacks and drinks are served. 
Accessibility: The Space is located on the second floor of a historic building, accessible via a flight of stairs. Unfortunately, there is no elevator access at this time. This means we are unable to accommodate wheelchairs or guests with significant mobility challenges. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.

title: SMC Trail Work Volunteer Day
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
**TRAIL WORK will continue rerouting the Hogenauer Trail** (we are almost finished!) up the slope and away from recently installed property fences. **Meet At:** Dog Park/ Wildflower Preserve, 11 Bear Lane, Maplewood. From there, we will walk to Crater View on Crest drive and then to the Hogenauer trail work site.

Trail work is physically challenging but very satisfying as we use hand tools to build and repair trails. Participants must be 15+ years. Those younger than 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Participants **should wear long pants** due to [ticks](https://www.somocon.org/?page_id=193928&fb) and thron bushes and sturdy shoes, and bring gloves (though backup gloves will be available). Tools, water, and a snack will be provided. (Registration is not required though if you sign up on Meetup, it helps us know how many tools to bring.) Only heavy, steady rain cancels.

title: Folk & Blues with Tal Naccarato
description:
About the program

Tal Naccarato performs solo acoustic music from his original and traditional repertoire as a singer-songwriter and guitarist in the Americana, folk, and blues genres. Rare vintage instruments are demonstrated during the performance, along with talks about the various musical genres. 

 

About the artist

Tal Naccarato is a vibrant composer, songwriter, and teaching artist whose roots stretch from the medieval mountain village of Fiumefreddo, Bruzio, Italy, to the vibrant community of East Flatbush, Brooklyn. His original music is a mix of folk, Americana, rock, and blues, mixed with classical guitar elements and a distinct bluesy swing. Tal was the first-place winner in the Long Island Blues Society Solo/Duo Competition in 2023. He performs solo acoustic shows, both with original music and traditional songs.

title: Chamber Opera Performance: "L'enfant et les Sortilèges"
description:
Maurice Ravel’s L’enfant et les sortilèges is a wildly imaginative fantasy opera where a single child’s tantrum sets an entire enchanted world into motion. In a flash of frustration, the ordinary becomes extraordinary—walls start to whisper, teacups burst into song, animals argue back, and the child’s room transforms into a living, breathing world of magic and mischief.
As this fantastical realm awakens, the child is swept into a dazzling swirl of musical surprises and unexpected voices, where every object has something to say and nothing is quite as it seems. With Ravel’s shimmering, kaleidoscopic score at its heart, this enchanting opera is a playful journey through wonder, chaos, and the power of imagination to transform everything it touches.
(Sung in French with English Surtitles~ runtime: approx 1 hour)
Montclair State University Students FREE with ID at Kasser Box Office

Hosted by: The College of the Arts

Additional Information can be found at: https://montclair.campuslabs.com/engage/event/12657859

description:
Civic Leadership and SEL: Lessons from NJ Changemakers invites educators to explore how the powerful, personal stories of New Jersey Hall of Fame inductees can serve as catalysts for meaningful social-emotional learning and authentic civic engagement in today’s classrooms. By examining moments of courage, empathy, advocacy, and ethical decision-making in the lives of New Jersey leaders, educators will uncover practical ways to help students build self-awareness, social awareness, and a sense of agency.
Drawing from the lives and legacies of Peter J. McGuire (Father of Labor Day), Dorothea Dix (mental health reformer), David Mixner (political activist, author, and playwright), and Clara Maass (public health pioneer), participants will analyze how these changemakers confronted injustice, advocated for vulnerable communities, and took action in times of social and public health crises—making abstract concepts such as fairness, wellness, and justice tangible and relevant for students. 
Educators will compare and contrast AI-powered lesson generators, including MagicSchool and Curipod, and create SEL or civic action lessons and student activities using inductee stories, leveraging AI scaffolding to differentiate instruction for diverse learners. This workshop empowers educators to transform local legends into catalysts for empathy, critical thinking, and civic participation—helping all students see themselves as the next generation of changemakers.

description:
An American tall tale with a surprising plot and the heart of a giant. Gabriel Fisher is born an orphan, weighing 18 pounds and measuring 27 inches long. Gabriel gets taken in by his devout Amish grandparents who try to protect him from the "English" world. But it’s hard to hide when you’re nearly 8 feet tall. When Gabriel reaches 17, the local football coach spots him tossing hay bales like sofa cushions. What happens next transforms not only Gabriel’s life but the lives of everyone he meets. 



"'Life, and Death, and Giants' is an intriguing and alluring novel from beginning to end....Reading it is like meeting a family that you never knew existed and becoming close friends in a few weeks. Highly recommended." --Jane Smiley



RON RINDO is a professor of English and creative writing at the University of Wisconsin-Oshkosh. He has published one previous novel, "Breathing Lake Superior, "and three short story collections. He lives in Pickett, Wisconsin.

title: Exile, Memory, and the Meaning of Home: A Conversation with Ana Hebra Flaster
description:
What happens when the country you love forces you out, leaving you just 48 hours to abandon everything you’ve ever known? Join us online for an extraordinary online conversation with author and essayist Ana Hebra Flaster as we discuss her sweeping yet deeply intimate memoir Property of the Revolution: From a Cuban Barrio to a New Hampshire Mill Town.

Ana Hebra Flaster was six years old when her working-class family was kicked out of their Havana barrio for opposing communism. Once devoted revolutionaries themselves but disillusioned by the Castro government’s repressive tactics, they fled to the US. The permanent losses they suffered—of home, country, and loved ones, all within forty-eight hours—haunted her multigenerational family as they reclaimed their lives and freedom in 1967 New Hampshire. There, they fed each other stories of their scrappy barrio—some of which Hebra Flaster has shared on All Things Considered—to resurrect their lost world and fortify themselves for a daunting task: building a new life in a foreign land.

Weaving pivotal events in Cuba–US history with her viejos’—elders’—stories of surviving political upheaval, impossible choices, and “refugeedom,” Property of the Revolution celebrates the indomitable spirit and wisdom of the women warriors who led the family out of Cuba, shaped its rebirth as Cuban Americans, and helped Ana grow up hopeful, future-facing—American. But what happens when deeply buried childhood memories resurface, demanding an adult’s reckoning?

Here’s how the fiercest love, the most stubborn will, and the power of family put nine new Americans back on their feet.

Register today to gain a deeper, more personal perspective on the refugee experience and the enduring quest to define home.

 

About the Author: 

Ana Hebra Flaster is journalist and the author of Property of the Revolution: From a Cuban Barrio to a New Hampshire Mill Town, published in April 2025 (She Writes Press, Simon and Schuster distribution). A former child-refugee from Cuba, Ana’s work has appeared in national print and online media, including: The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, The Washington Post, and The Boston Globe. Her commentaries and storytelling have aired on NPR’s All Things Considered and PBS’s Stories from the Stage. Since its publication in April 2025, Property of the Revolution has won first place in several international writing contests, including: 2026 IBPA Book Awards (Memoir); 2025 Discovery Book Awards (Nonfiction overall); 2025 International Book Awards (Creative Nonfiction), and the 2025 IAP Book Awards (Memoir of the Year). The memoir was selected as the Nashua, New Hampshire, 2026 All-City Read and the Rivier University 2025 First-Year Read. Ana speaks regularly with student, library, and civic groups about her family’s journey and the refugee and immigrant experience. She is currently focused on covering the struggle for democracy and human rights in Cuba in her weekly Substack, CubaCurious, a project she launched in July 2024.

title: Library Speakers Consortium - Exile, Memory, and the Meaning of Home: A Conversation with Ana Hebra Flaster
description:
You must register here to attend:  https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/225105



What happens when the country you love forces you out, leaving you just 48 hours to abandon everything you’ve ever known? Join us online for an extraordinary online conversation with author and essayist Ana Hebra Flaster as we discuss her sweeping yet deeply intimate memoir Property of the Revolution: From a Cuban Barrio to a New Hampshire Mill Town.

Ana Hebra Flaster was six years old when her working-class family was kicked out of their Havana barrio for opposing communism. Once devoted revolutionaries themselves but disillusioned by the Castro government’s repressive tactics, they fled to the US. The permanent losses they suffered—of home, country, and loved ones, all within forty-eight hours—haunted her multigenerational family as they reclaimed their lives and freedom in 1967 New Hampshire. There, they fed each other stories of their scrappy barrio—some of which Hebra Flaster has shared on All Things Considered—to resurrect their lost world and fortify themselves for a daunting task: building a new life in a foreign land.

Weaving pivotal events in Cuba–US history with her viejos’—elders’—stories of surviving political upheaval, impossible choices, and “refugeedom,” Property of the Revolution celebrates the indomitable spirit and wisdom of the women warriors who led the family out of Cuba, shaped its rebirth as Cuban Americans, and helped Ana grow up hopeful, future-facing—American. But what happens when deeply buried childhood memories resurface, demanding an adult’s reckoning?

Here’s how the fiercest love, the most stubborn will, and the power of family put nine new Americans back on their feet.

Register today to gain a deeper, more personal perspective on the refugee experience and the enduring quest to define home.

About the Author: 

Ana Hebra Flaster is journalist and the author of Property of the Revolution: From a Cuban Barrio to a New Hampshire Mill Town, published in April 2025 (She Writes Press, Simon and Schuster distribution). A former child-refugee from Cuba, Ana’s work has appeared in national print and online media, including: The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, The Washington Post, and The Boston Globe. Her commentaries and storytelling have aired on NPR’s All Things Considered and PBS’s Stories from the Stage. Since its publication in April 2025, Property of the Revolution has won first place in several international writing contests, including: 2026 IBPA Book Awards (Memoir); 2025 Discovery Book Awards (Nonfiction overall); 2025 International Book Awards (Creative Nonfiction), and the 2025 IAP Book Awards (Memoir of the Year). The memoir was selected as the Nashua, New Hampshire, 2026 All-City Read and the Rivier University 2025 First-Year Read. Ana speaks regularly with student, library, and civic groups about her family’s journey and the refugee and immigrant experience. She is currently focused on covering the struggle for democracy and human rights in Cuba in her weekly Substack, CubaCurious, a project she launched in July 2024.

title: Tech Talks: The Year in Tech: 2026 in Review
description:
Tech Talks is a free informational series where library staff introduce and explain the technology topics that matter most in today's digital world. Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.

All are welcome regardless of experience level, and time is reserved at the end of each session for Q&A. Sessions are free and open to the public.

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Women and Money Roundtable - How to Make Sense of Today's Financial Markets
description:
A virtual, lively, and informative discussion on today’s financial markets and how they might fit into your portfolio. 


Julia Strayer and Liz Maccarone will lead a lively and informative discussion on today’s financial markets and how they might fit into your portfolio.

This is a virtual program that takes place over Zoom. As the date approaches, you will receive an email with the Zoom link.

About the Presenters

Julia Strayer, CPWA®, CIMA®, CRPC® Senior Vice President, Wealth Management Advisor.  Prior to joining Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2000, Julia was a vice president and private banker for BankBoston’s Private Bank for 7 years, responsible for asset management and trust services. Previously, Julia worked in marketing for 9 years with Merrill. Julia has a BA from Ohio State University and an MBA from New York University’s Stern School of Business. Julia has appeared on the CNBC show “Power Lunch,” CBS “This Morning,” WGCH’s “Women in Business,” in addition to featured articles in USA Today.

Liz Maccarone, CRPC® Senior Financial Advisor.  Liz joined Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2012. Liz works closely with high-net-worth individuals and their families to create personalized and comprehensive strategies that support their goals, including investment management, retirement planning, liability management, and multigenerational planning. Liz values the importance of establishing and cultivating relationships with families including the next generation. Liz graduated from Fairfield University with a dual bachelor’s degree in Finance and Marketing. She began her career working at a boutique investment firm as a Business Development Associate, specializing in commodities and futures trading.

title: Comic Strips and Kimchi: Cooking Korean Food Made Easy with Robin Ha
description:
Cooking authentic Korean food at home doesn't have to be intimidating or complicated—in fact, it can be as fun and engaging as reading your favorite graphic novel! Join us for a virtual conversation with artist and author Robin Ha as we explore her New York Times bestselling book, Cook Korean!: A Comic Book Cookbook.

Fun to look at and easy to use, this unique combination of cookbook and graphic novel is the ideal introduction to cooking Korean cuisine at home. Robin Ha’s colorful and humorous one-to three-page comics fully illustrate the steps and ingredients needed to bring more than sixty traditional (and some not-so-traditional) dishes to life.

In these playful but exact recipes, you’ll learn how to create everything from easy kimchi (mak kimchi) and soy garlic beef over rice (bulgogi dupbap) to seaweed rice rolls (gimbap) and beyond. Friendly and inviting, Cook Korean! is perfect for beginners and seasoned cooks alike.

Each chapter includes personal anecdotes and cultural insights from Ha, providing an intimate entry point for those looking to try their hand at this cuisine.

Register today to discover how easy, approachable, and fun authentic Korean cooking can be!

 

About the Author: 

Robin Ha is the New York Times bestselling author and illustrator of Cook Korean!: A Comic Book with Recipes, as well as the graphic novel memoir Almost American Girl and historical fantasy graphic novel The Fox Maidens. Her comics and illustrations have also appeared in various publications, including The Washington Post and The Los Angeles Times, as well as in anthologies highlighting Asian American culture: Rise: A Pop History of Asian America from the Nineties to Now, New Frontiers: The Many Worlds of George Takei, and Shattered: The Asian American Comics Anthology (Secret Identities). Robin grew up reading and drawing comics. At fourteen she moved to the United States from Seoul, Korea. She studied illustration at Rhode Island School of Design. She now lives in Virginia.

title: Astrology 101: What's Your Sign?
location: Nutley - Stockton Room, Nutley Free Public Library
description:
Thursday, December 10, 2026 from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM.

No registration required! 

Let's talk astrology! This program will provide a basic overview of Western astrology, including the twelve zodiac signs, the four elements and three modalities, the ten traditional planets, and the five major aspects.

This program is a lecture-style PowerPoint presentation with Q&A woven throughout. The focus here is not on "sun sign astrology" (analyzing personalities based simply on the twelve zodiac signs), but rather on gaining a bird's eye view of the larger astrological system, of which sun signs are just one part. You will leave the program with the information you need to look at an astrology chart and decode its many glyphs — the ancient symbols that represent the key foundational concepts of this archetypal language.

Attendees are strongly encouraged to look up their natal charts in advance on any number of free websites. Although Kate will not have time to provide personalized chart interpretations, you will be invited to apply key concepts to your own chart as we go. (Hard copy or digital is fine.)  You may also want to bring a notebook and pen. While Astrology 101 is designed with total beginners in mind, some familiarity with the twelve zodiac signs, especially your own sign, is helpful. More intermediate astrology learners may benefit from this jam-packed review of foundational concepts. 

More about natal charts: The phrase "natal chart" involves using not only the day of your birth, but also the exact place and the exact time of your birth, in order to look at your Sun, Moon, Rising as well as the traditional planets Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, and the modern planets Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto. Anyone who does not know and cannot access their exact time of birth can still get a lot out of Astrology 101. They can look up everything apart from the rising/ascendant sign. Below is an example chart generated by the free website astro.com! You can bring a print out or digital copy of your chart to the program!



 

About the presenter: Kate Sheridan, a.k.a. The Laundress, is a tarot reader and astrologer who believes that each one of us can make our own magic. Her approach is healing rather than predictive, and her work is deeply informed by Jungian psychology. You can find her on Instagram @themodernlaundress or online at thelaundresstarot.com.

title: Washington's Crossing: 1776
description:
An America 250 Program

Historian Glenn LeBoeuf explains how General Washington’s audacious bets at Trenton and Princeton salvaged the freedom cause.

About the program

By the winter of 1776, Washington’s army had shrunk from its high of almost 31,000 to about 3,500 in December. Many politicians were demanding Washington's replacement, but those who had stuck by him through the bitter defeats on Long Island and Manhattan and the swift retreat across New Jersey to the relative safety of Pennsylvania remained committed to the cause of independence. Come for the stories of these heroic troops and the numerous political, logistical, topographical, and tactical problems they faced. Above all, come hear about the leader who inspired them: Washington's soldiers would not quit this cause or this man. If you have never heard Glenn speak, strap in for a fantastic experience!

About the presenter

Since 1984, Glenn LeBoeuf has lectured on history and biography, emphasizing the personalities of George Washington and Abraham Lincoln. His research has helped us understand their leadership styles and the historical contexts in which they operated, and his teaching methods have inspired many students to explore the complexities of American history.

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

As always, we will go at a moderate pace and won’t leave anyone behind. But please be considerate of others if you don't think you will be able to hike/walk at a moderate pace for the duration.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: Bowling Night - Montvale
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
This is an event for casual bowling at Montvale Lanes, 14 W. Grand Ave. All are welcome for **two games, food and drinks**, and any post- or pre-game hang out. Show up anytime! Questions or comments? You can message Andy Milone on Meetup, or call/text him at **201-234-9609**.

\*\*\* Before bowling, we might stop by the Pizza Parlour, 6 S. Kinderkamack Road in Montvale, for a few slices. Post a comment on the event page to gauge interest. **After bowling, we'll definitely be heading to The Ridge Diner, 125 Kinderkamack Road in Park Ridge, at 10:15 p.m. for some food and/or drinks.** \*\*\*

About the group: People of all ages, backgrounds and abilities are welcome! We're not professionals and we're not in a league. In fact, we're a group of people who probably each won't score more than 100 points and will land more than our fair share of gutter balls. There's no pressure at all!!!! We're not here to analyze your form or technique.

More event details: You pay for your own games, food and drinks. Please bring cash. The alley does not accept card. But there is an ATM on site. **The** **cost per player is $18 for two games** **and bowling shoes.** If you have your own shoes, the cost is $12. Please try to bring exact change since Andy will have a limited amount of cash. If you bring a $20 bill and he doesn't have change, any remainder would just go toward the bowling alley tip.

Food and drinks (alcoholic and non-alcoholic) are available on site, plus tables and an alley bar to hang at during the event. There is a dart board and a few arcade games, as well.

**What do you do when you get there?** Find the group inside around the front desk. Look for a growing group of people! Call or text Andy Milone at 201-234-9609 if you can't find us. Once Andy secures the lanes, please pay him before getting your bowling shoes and heading to the lanes.

**Please know that it is possible we have to wait 20-40 minutes until lane(s) free up.** It's also possible that we may have to relocate or cancel that night if there's a long wait list upon arrival. Please keep that in mind if traveling from far away!

For those who don't have cars or are looking to avoid driving, the Montvale Train Station is only like a five-minute walk from the bowling alley and can be reached via the Pascack Valley Line. Last train leaves at 12:20 a.m. and heads toward Hoboken. (https://gmtma.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/11/rail_system_map.jpg)

Many thanks to Taylor, one of our group participants, for recommending Montvale Lanes! You can learn more at: www.montvalelanes.com.

Hope you'll join us for our 28th bowling event, or consider attending one of our volleyball, tennis or other activities -> www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball

If interested in staying in touch with group members or conversing about future events, feel free to inquire about our WhatsApp group chat.
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: NJ Code & Coffee - December meetup
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the monthly **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

\*your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,

* What you can help others with,
\*What you would like help with,
* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

**Community Discord - come hang out before and after!:**
[www.codeandcoffee.chat](www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming and a powerful network.

Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, and a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate and build with. The next wave in enterprises is being born within their walls. Become a part of the story: [EqualSpace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

Is your React app slow, and you're not sure why? Join us for a hands-on talk on React performance — no theory-only slides, every claim gets proven live.

**Doors open at 2pm, talk starts at 3pm, arrive early for networking and light refreshments.**

Join the NJ Code & Coffee Community Discord - come hang out before and after:

Come close out 2026 at the Pollinator Meadow! Bring warm drinks to cheers and celebrate as we complete a gentle path through the meadow. This is a great time for volunteers to return to see how far the meadow has come.

Work is strenuous to moderate. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

title: Hike with Dr. Kirk! 3-4 miles
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Sunday Dec 13, 2-4:30 pm. Free expert-led hike in South Mountain Reservation. Hike about 2-3 hours covering 3-4 miles at a modest pace over rocky trails with one long climb from the Rahway River up South Mountain. Focus on ecology and hydrology, led by Dr. Kirk Barrett, President of the Rahway Watershed Association and expert on local watershed issues. Good balance required. Children welcome. No dogs. Co-Sponsored by the South Mountain Conservancy and the Rahway River Watershed Association. Meet at Clipper Pavilion in South Mountain Reservation on Cherry Lane in West Orange (not at McLoone's). Steady rain cancels. Email president@rahwayriver.org with questions.

Advance registration required via [rahwayriver.org/calendar.html](rahwayriver.org/calendar.html) . Email president@rahwayriver.org with questions.

I also understand that by signing below I approve the possible use of photos of me at this SMC event on social media or in promotional materials.

**BY REGISTERING FOR THIS HIKE I attest I am in good health and attest that I: Am not experiencing any symptoms of illness such as cough, shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, fever, chills, repeated shaking with chills, muscle pain, headache, sore throat, or new loss of taste or smell.**
**Am following all CDC recommended guidelines, above, and limiting my exposure to the novel coronavirus/COVID-19.**
\# Arrival\, Weather\, & Cancellations
Please come to the starting point 10 minutes ahead of time so the hike can start promptly. Times are our best estimates; they can vary depending on conditions, and the size and pace of a group. If you have any questions, call the leader. **Temperatures above 90 degrees and steady rain cancels, but intermittent drizzle does not. You will *not* be notified.** **Bring water. title: Laugh-Out-Loud Nostalgia: Bringing Junie B. Jones to Life in Comics with Colleen AF Venable
description:
Generations of readers grew up laughing with the world’s funniest kid, and now she’s back in a vibrant, visual format! Join us for a lively virtual conversation with National Book Award finalist Colleen AF Venable as we explore her acclaimed comic adaptations in Junie B. Jones: A Graphic Novel.

Bringing Barbara Park’s beloved, spunky first-grader into full-color comic panels, Colleen captures all the energy, humor, and heart of the original series for both nostalgic fans and a new generation of readers. 

Discover how Colleen translated Barbara Park's beloved chapter books into dynamic graphic novel scripts while honoring the original spirit, and learn how text and comic art work together to bring Junie B.'s hilarious expressions and schoolyard misadventures to life.

Register today and discover how visual storytelling keeps classic stories alive for readers of all ages!

 

About the Author: 

COLLEEN AF (Ann Felicity) VENABLE is the author of many kids books, including the Katie the Catsitter series. Colleen discovered Junie B. as a young babysitter and says, "I don't think any character in literature connects with me as much!"

title: Holiday New York City Hike!
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for our annual Holiday New York City Hike!
This year, we'll meet at New York Penn Station, in the mall type area with the large Christmas tree like we usually do (it's in the cover photo here).
This would be the big circular area in NY Penn Station.
From there, we'll all take the subway north to Van Cortland Park, Bronx, and we'll start with a bunch of the trails there we've never done before.
From there, we head west toward the Hudson River where we'll begin heading south on some of the trails and walkways.
We'll walk the newly reopened pedestrian lanes over Henry Hudson Bridge and then follow slopes though Inwood Hills Park and Fort Tryon Park.
After this, we'll try to take the Hudson River Greenway and Empire State Trail, but keep to the more middle section of it. We've done the upper and lower bits in the past, so this is an opportunity to do some of the other middle ground.
We're planning on doing about fifteen miles, but in the city, people can cut out just about any time with all of the public transportation.
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374
NOTE that when you arrive, use the restroom right away. Every year, we end up waiting around, and then after waiting around and we're about ready to go, everyone decides they want to use the restroom. Don't do that!

title: Mental Health Support Group (NAMI's Connection Recovery Peer Support Group)
description:
The Essex-Passaic Chapter of NAMI (The National Alliance on Mental Illness) Connection Recovery Peer Support Group Program meets on the 4th Tuesday of each month at the West Caldwell Library on 30 Clinton Road. 

NAMI is the most influential organization devoted to helping people with mental illness and their relatives and loved ones recover and deal with mental health issues. These meetings will be led by people having some form of mental illness. During these meetings, we will conduct peer support though all people interested in this organization are encouraged to attend. You do not have to sign up in advance. All meetings are kept confidential and are led by people specifically trained to conduct these meetings.

 NAMI Connection is a recovery peer support group program that offers respect, understanding, encouragement and hope. NAMI Connection groups are:

·       Free and confidential

·       Held monthly for 90 minutes  

·       Designed to connect, encourage, and support participants using a structured support group model

·       Led by trained facilitators living in recovery themselves

This meeting is for anyone ages 18  who is dealing with their own mental illness or a loved one's.  

 

https://nami.org/Home

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

As always, we will go at a moderate pace and won’t leave anyone behind. But please be considerate of others if you don't think you will be able to hike/walk at a moderate pace for the duration.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: First Day Phillipsburg Easton Hike!
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this big loop hike featuring Easton and Phillipsburg!
It has become a tradition doing this area as part of the New Year, starting it off right with walking!
This year, we'll do trails and historic sites all around both Easton and Phillipsburg, and we'll start in Easton at the Giant Supermarket just off of Sullivan Trail.
We'll walk some back streets for a bit tracing the historic route of the area trolley. This will lead us into Gollub Park where we will visit the former site of the Paxinosa Inn, and then make our way down along the trolley bed as it weaves around past St Anthony's Nose, then return to the streets.
We'll pass through the college campus and down the giant steps that have been repaired recently, then head across the Rt 22 bridge to Phillipsburg.
We'll follow Warren Highlands Trail route and possibly just take in South Main Street past the historic railroad features. If your friends at any of these locations are around, we'll be sure to stop in!
We continue from here across the black bridge and over to the former Morris Canal basin and Mt Parnassus. Depending on time, we may go up the mountain for the view.
We'll make our way along the former Morris Canal back toward Union Square where we will cross the Northampton Street Free Bridge into Easton.
Next, we follow greenways west into town, mostly rail beds, then north on the Easton and Northern line. We'll turn off and get on more of the Two Rivers Trailways to get back to Giant.
Total distance should be 15 miles.
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

description:

Join us online for a hilarious, action-packed virtual conversation with #1 international bestselling author Jeff Kinney as he introduces the 21st book in his globally beloved series, Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Fight or Flight. 

Greg Heffley is about to learn that surviving middle school is no easy feat.

In Fight or Flight, Greg’s hard-earned expertise on navigating the rough-and-tumble world of middle school is put to the test.

When a secret binder filled with Greg’s notes on the school’s biggest bullies falls into the wrong hands, his world quickly begins to unravel. Now it’s a race against time before the truth comes out. Will Greg throw in the towel—or go down swinging?

Complete with Kinney's signature comic illustrations and sharp, laugh-out-loud humor, this latest installment captures the awkward, unpredictable realities of growing up that have made Greg Heffley an icon for generations of readers.

Register today to gain exclusive, behind-the-scenes access to Jeff Kinney’s creative universe! 

About the Author: 

Jeff Kinney is a #1 New York Times bestselling author, a six-time Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Award winner for Favorite Book, and one of Time magazine's 100 Most Influential People in the World. He spent his childhood in the Washington, D.C., area and later moved to Massachusetts, where he and his family own a bookstore called An Unlikely Story.

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

A Conversation led by Rabbi Justus Baird  
  
In this three-part learning series, we will explore multiple narratives of the last century of events in Israel/Palestine, specifically from Israeli Jewish and Palestinian points of view. title: Flavor, Heritage, and Connection to the Land: Exploring Indigenous Foods with Sean Sherman
description:
Join us for an online conversation with acclaimed Oglala Lakota chef Sean Sherman as he talks about Turtle Island: Foods and Traditions of the Indigenous Peoples of North America, a national bestseller named one of the year’s best cookbooks by The New York Times, The Washington Post, Smithsonian Magazine, and Library Journal.

Growing up on South Dakota’s Pine Ridge Reservation, Oglala Lakota chef Sean Sherman understood that his people’s food was rich in flavor, heritage, and connection to the land. It was in the midst of a successful restaurant career mainly cooking European cuisines that he realized the lack of understanding about Native American foodways—a revelation that sent him on a journey to learn more about how Indigenous communities have preserved and evolved their cuisines through the centuries. Now a leading figure in the Indigenous food movement, he shares in Turtle Island the unique and diverse Native foodways of North America through both traditional and modern recipes made with ingredients that have nourished Indigenous peoples physically, spiritually, and culturally for generations.

Organized by region, this book delves into the rich culinary landscapes of Turtle Island—as many Indigenous cultures call this continent. Learn to eat with the seasons, consume meat and fish nose-to-tail, focus on plant-forward dishes, and discover how to better feed yourself. 

Exemplifying how Native foodways can teach us all to connect with the natural world around us, Turtle Island features rich narrative histories and spotlights the communities producing, gathering, and cooking these foods, including remarkable stories of ingenuity and adaptation that capture the resilience of Indigenous communities.

Register now and immerse yourself in the history (and delicious recipes) of Native American cuisine, told directly by one of the most influential chefs working today.

 

About the Author:

Chef Sean Sherman has dedicated his career to supporting Indigenous food systems and advancing Native food sovereignty. Through his advocacy, education, and culinary leadership, Sean works to reclaim and celebrate the rich food traditions of Indigenous communities throughout North America while advancing a more equitable and sustainable food future.

As founder and Executive Director of North American Traditional Indigenous Food Systems (NATIFS), he leads efforts to revitalize Indigenous foodways through education,workforce development, and Indigenous food enterprises.

Sean’s first book, The Sioux Chef's Indigenous Kitchen, received the James Beard Award for Best American Cookbook in 2018. He was also honored with the James Beard Foundation's Leadership Award in 2019, and in 2021, he opened Owamni by The Sioux Chef, Minnesota's first full-service Indigenous restaurant, which has earned numerous accolades, including the James Beard Foundation's 2022 award for Best New Restaurant in America. In 2023, Sean was recognized as one of TIME magazine's 100 Most Influential People and received the ninth annual Julia Child Award for his leadership, innovation, and advocacy in transforming Indigenous cuisine. His most recent book, Turtle Island: Foods and Traditions of the Indigenous Peoples of North America, was nominated for a James Beard Award.

location: Glen Ridge - Meeting Room, Glen Ridge Free Public Library
description:
This program is designed to provide caregivers with a comprehensive overview of Alzheimer’s disease and other types of dementia. Caregivers of individuals with dementia will learn about the various stages of Alzheimer’s disease, the process of getting a diagnosis, strategies for caring for someone with dementia, and much more.

Adult Program | in-person | RSVP requested*
*Open to ALL
